scenes.title: Cold open
narration: During droughts, women perform this dance at midnight while chanting Vedic mantras to summon Lord Indra, the god of rain, to end agricultural crises.
This is Jatjatin Dance. Ancient tradition.
on_screen: Title card: Jatjatin Dance · India and Nepal · Ancient tradition

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Jatjatin is an ancient tradition of the Mithila region, practiced for generations across northern Bihar and southern Nepal.
It is rooted in the agricultural realities of the plains, where the timing of the monsoon dictates both the survival of crops and the migration patterns of the workforce.
on_screen: Map: India and Nepal · South Asia

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance serves two main purposes: depicting the emotional narrative of a couple's separation due to work migration and acting as a religious ritual to appease Lord Indra during times of drought.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed as a duet featuring circular footwork.
The female performer uses her dupatta (scarf) to symbolize weeping, moving it in a fluttering motion around the male performer.
The movements are expressive and symbolic, designed to reflect the narrative of a couple's impending separation or, in ritual contexts, the community's hope for rain.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The performance is driven by the rhythmic sounds of the dholak (drum) and manjira (cymbals).
The accompanying songs, known as Jat-Jatin songs, are often plaintive in tone and may be interspersed with Vedic mantras during ritual performances.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers typically wear traditional Mithila attire.
A key element for the female dancer is the dupatta, which is used as a prop to convey emotion.
Narrative performances occur during the monsoon, while ritual performances take place at midnight in outdoor settings during droughts.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The sources do not name specific individual dancers or choreographers, as it is a traditional folk form practiced by the community.
The dance is found throughout the Mithila region, spanning both southern Nepal and northern Bihar, India.
The dance is part of the broader folk traditions of Nepal and Bihar, specifically tied to the Mithila cultural identity.

images.description: Jat Jatin is the dance of women of the Mithila region of Bihar and is supposed to be performed on moonlit nights during the monsoons. Grown-up girls and young housewives assemble in the courtyard and, accompanied by a drum, dance from midnight to dawn. As they dance, they enact in gestures the epic story of the love of Jata and Jatin. The most dramatic episode of the dance concerns a wicked boatma
